summary: The author stopped the extracts at two days and asked for a measure of the centrality of tables, other measures in that vein, and whether to tell core, descriptive and linking tables apart.
verbatim: No let's keep it at this for now. I don't expect anything structural from it, at most we'll see data problems, but that is not the main point of this analysis, although it is important of course to model later on. I have another question, that has not been addressed up til now, but which is in my opinion important in understanding the structure of the data. We have not said anything yet about the (network) centrality of the tables. There are tables that are more important and those that are less important, or core tables and peripheral tables. Can you think of a measure of the centrality of the tables (maybe using graph theory). Do you agree that centrality is an important measure to understand when starting modelling later on? Are there other measures that are important to understand in this vein? Do you agree with making a distinction between core tables, descriptive tables (like list of values, look up tables), and linking tables?
